title: HCP — Report Onward Sharing — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Report onward sharing operation (HCP 5.2.8; `POST /v2/shares` in HCP 9.2): an HCP Client tells the provider what context it shared with another organization. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

recipient.description: HCP `recipient`: the organization the client told (HCP 5.2.8). Not the document's own `recipient`, which is the HCP Provider.

refs.description: HCP `refs`: the `ref` of each entry the client drew on (HCP 5.2.8, 7.4). The bound of 256, and each item's maxLength, are framework bounds, not HCP requirements.

purpose.description: HCP `purpose`: the purpose code of the share, one of the authorization detail's purposes (HCP 5.2.8, 6.1.5.2).

accessToken.description: The HCP access token for the grant under which the client acts (HCP 12, 13), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP binding sends it as a Bearer token (HCP 9.3); this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque.

domain.description: Its DNS domain, which the provider checks against the detail's `domains` and `notTo` (HCP 5.2.8, 6.1.5).

name.description: A name the person can recognize (HCP 5.2.8).

Response.title: HCP — Report Onward Sharing — response payload
Response.description: The report is recorded and the share was one the grant allowed. HCP defines no result and its HTTP binding answers `204 No Content` (HCP 5.2.8, 9.4.16), so the payload is the empty object. A share the grant did not allow is recorded all the same and answered with trust-task-error `permissionDenied`.
